blocks.text: 当Notable Capital把其10亿美元基金美国部分的约10%投入Anthropic的E轮融资时，许多有限合伙人（LP）对这笔巨额押注感到困惑。Claude的开发商当时仍落后于最大竞争对手OpenAI，而DeepSeek几周前刚发布R1模型，大有赶超闭源对手之势。此外，Anthropic估值高达615亿美元，是这家以早期投资为主的风投机构25年历史中投过的估值最高的公司。

inlines.text: 当Notable Capital把其10亿美元基金美国部分的约10%投入Anthropic的E轮融资时，许多有限合伙人（LP）对这笔巨额押注感到困惑。Claude的开发商当时仍落后于最大竞争对手OpenAI，而DeepSeek几周前刚发布R1模型，大有赶超闭源对手之势。此外，Anthropic估值高达615亿美元，是这家以早期投资为主的风投机构25年历史中投过的估值最高的公司。

blocks.text: 但Notable的投资人看好Anthropic的未来。这家机构原名为GGV Capital，2024年与中国业务分拆。由管理合伙人Hans Tung（童士豪）、Glenn Solomon和投资经理Dan Cahana组成的团队分析数据后发现，开发者越来越偏爱Claude而非ChatGPT，使用Claude的时间占比达70%，与前一年相比出现逆转。

blocks.text: 新加坡主权财富基金GIC在整个2024年一直在研究Anthropic，但直到2025年初，该基金科技投资主管Chris Emanuel在旧金山意大利餐厅Che Fico与Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao会面后，才做出首笔投资。Rao展示了模型改进如何推动企业采用率上升，激发了Emanuel的兴趣。GIC随后在Anthropic的F轮融资中首次投资，该轮于2025年9月宣布，估值1830亿美元。

blocks.text: “Claude Code当时刚发布，”Emanuel对TechCrunch表示。“虽然还很早期，但即便那时我们也能看到它深受开发者欢迎的迹象。”GIC对这家AI实验室的信心极高，后来与Coatue共同领投了Anthropic估值3800亿美元的G轮融资，并在估值9650亿美元的IPO前轮次中再次作为联合领投方之一回归。据一位了解GIC财务情况的人士称，GIC在三轮融资中向Anthropic投资超过45亿美元，IPO后持股约相当于公司1%。

blocks.text: When Notable Capital poured roughly 10% of the U.S. portion of its $1 billion-plus fund into Anthropic’s Series E, many limited partners were perplexed by the massive bet. Claude’s maker was still trailing its biggest rival, OpenAI, and DeepSeek had released its R1 model just weeks earlier, threatening to overtake closed-source competitors. Moreover, at $61.5 billion, Anthropic’s valuation was by far the highest that the predominantly early-stage venture firm had invested at in its 25-year history.

blocks.text: But investors at Notable, formerly known as GGV Capital before its 2024 split from its China operations, were confident in Anthropic’s future. A team that included managing partners Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon and principal Dan Cahana crunched the numbers and found that developers were increasingly favoring Claude over ChatGPT, using Claude 70% of the time, a reversal from the previous year.

On Wednesday, Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest IPO in history, reaching a fully diluted valuation of about $1.5 trillion before its shares began trading the next day, a paper return of roughly 15 times.

blocks.text: Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC had been researching Anthropic throughout 2024, but it didn’t make its first investment until after Chris Emanuel, head of the fund’s tech investments, met with Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao at Che Fico, an Italian restaurant in San Francisco, in early 2025. Rao helped pique Emanuel’s interest in the company by showing that model improvements were driving rising enterprise adoption. GIC then made its first investment in Anthropic’s Series F, a round announced in September 2025 at a $183 billion valuation.

Rao helped pique Emanuel’s interest in the company by showing that model improvements were driving rising enterprise adoption. GIC then made its first investment in Anthropic’s Series F, a round announced in September 2025 at a $183 billion valuation.

blocks.text: “Claude Code was just released then,” Emanuel told TechCrunch. “It was very early, but even then, we could see signs that it was really popular with developers.” GIC’s conviction in the AI lab was so high that the fund later led Anthropic’s Series G alongside Coatue at a $380 billion valuation, and returned as one of the co-leads for the pre-IPO round at $965 billion. Across the three rounds, GIC invested more than $4.5 billion in Anthropic, amassing a stake equal to about 1% of the company after its IPO, according to a person familiar with GIC’s financials.

blocks.text: Lilian Li, who leads U.S. growth investments at Baillie Gifford, began studying Anthropic and speaking with its team nearly two years before first investing in the company’s Series F. Baillie Gifford invested in the Claude maker once it became clear that the company was “executing consistently” on its vision while generating strong revenue and “compelling gross margins,” Li told TechCrunch.
